summary: Second-order optimizers (e.g., Shampoo, SOAP) have emerged as compelling alternatives to Adam/AdamW and promise faster per-step convergence than AdamW in transformer training. However, they still remain costly in practice, and even SOAP still pays substantial optimizer-state memory and eigendecomposition overhead.
takeaways: Our empirical results support the claim that FOAM matches strong SOAP and Muon baselines in validation loss across scales of large language model (LLM) pre-training, uses half of SOAP's optimizer state, runs at Muon-class wall-clock time, and retains robustness across a three-fold learning-rate range.
However, they still remain costly in practice, and even SOAP still pays substantial optimizer-state memory and eigendecomposition overhead.
In this paper, we answer yes with a lightweight SOAP variant, Factored One-sided Adam-Moment (FOAM).
